wkplan-2026-07-20.title: Week of July 20–26
wkplan-2026-07-20.review: Week 1 calibration did its job, and you called the miss yourself: two journals flagged that 3 sets on the mains felt like too little volume. You're right — that's a calibration-week artifact (Week 1 of new lifts is deliberately 3 ramping sets to find your numbers), so the 4th work set comes back now that we have them. What you logged: Front Squat 135×5 ('pretty solid'), Incline Bench 145×6 ('significantly stronger'), Push Press 125×6 (you beat the 115 target), Paused DL 225×4 (you noted it needs another week and the knee felt iffy on the last set). So this week: all four mains → 4 work sets; incline bench and push press earn a small top-end nudge (150 / 130); deadlift HOLDS 225 with the 4th set adding only volume, and auto-drops to 205 if the knee complains. Warm-up sets are back on leg press (your ask) and hip thrust. On running — you quietly ran ~17.4 mi, not the 14 the plan asked, and your easy discipline is the best it's been (Sunday's 4-miler came in genuinely easy). So we formalize the progression you're already making: ~18.5 mi, one hard run (Tue, now 6×3 min), the rest strict Z2 — controlled, because the jump from your 12.4-mi deload is already steep and June's burnout is the thing to avoid. Calisthenics gets a real forward step too: push-ups locked at 20 (you moved there on your own), dips to 3 sets, a target to beat on max pull-ups. Big picture on your actual question: the deficit is what's getting you under 190, and it's working — you're ahead of pace. Lifting's job in a cut is to keep the muscle you have (enough volume + heavy loads), not to redline everything at once — that's exactly what re-creates a burnout when you're under-fueled. Next week (7/27) crosses 20 mi and is the last build before the Aug 3 deload.

wkplan-2026-07-06.review: Week 3 was a strong build: squat hit 200 (Good, though form loosened on the last rep), RDL exceeded to 205 but your back felt tight — noted. Bench nailed 190 (Good, 1-2 RIR held) and OHP got pushed to 125, but that turned into a push press — too heavy, pulling it back. Barbell row (145) and lat pulldown (150) both moved up and felt good. Deadlift hit a shockingly good 275, and switching goblet→front squat clearly worked (125, way more effort at the same reps) — keeping front squat going forward. Tuesday's hard run averaged HR 167 — that's expected and by design for your one hard session each week, not a red flag, but this week's version is trimmed to match the deload. Weekly mileage landed close to plan (~14 mi), acute:chronic ratio came out to ~1.37 (just over the 1.3 caution line), and this lands right on the Week-4 deload slot in the 3-4 week cadence — so mileage backs off ~30% and key lifts ease ~10-15% this week to bank recovery before the next build block. On your note that the run progression feels slow: understood — you handled ~30 mi/wk before, but that volume is exactly what preceded the crash driving this rebuild, so we're staying disciplined on the ramp for now; once this deload clears, the build rate picks back up. Added core variety per your ask (Bird Dog, Pallof Press, Woodchopper, Suitcase Carry mixed in, staples like Plank/Ab Wheel held). Weight trending well: 199.4→195.3 lb since 6/18, on pace for the mid-Aug goal. No HRV/sleep/resting-HR synced this week — worth checking your wearable sync if that continues.
